title.value: An Empirical Study of Example Forgetting During Deep Neural Network Learning
title.justification: The title of the paper is 'An Empirical Study of Example Forgetting During Deep Neural Network Learning' as it appears at the beginning of the document.
title.quote:
A N E MPIRICAL S TUDY OF E XAMPLE F ORGETTING
DURING D EEP N EURAL N ETWORK L EARNING

analysis.description: The paper investigates the dynamics of example forgetting during the training of deep neural networks on single classification tasks. It examines how and why certain examples are consistently forgotten and the impact that has on the learning process. The paper also explores the potential benefits of removing certain training examples based on their forgetting dynamics.

type.justification: The research paper is classified as empirical because it conducts experiments on multiple datasets (such as MNIST and CIFAR) to study the phenomenon of example forgetting in deep neural networks, rather than focusing on theoretical formulations.
type.quote: Our purpose is to study this phenomenon from an empirical standpoint and characterize its prevalence in different datasets and across different model architectures.

name.justification: The paper discusses learning dynamics in neural networks, a core topic in deep learning research.
name.quote: Many machine learning models, in particular neural networks, cannot perform continual learning.

name.justification: The research draws inspiration from the phenomenon of catastrophic forgetting, a central problem in continual learning.
name.quote:
Many machine learning models, in particular neural networks, cannot perform continual learning.
They have a tendency to forget previously learnt information when trained on new tasks, a phe-
nomenon usually called catastrophic forgetting.

name.justification: The experiments in the paper involve computer vision datasets such as CIFAR-10 and MNIST.
name.quote: Our experimental evaluation on three datasets of increasing complexity: MNIST (LeCun et al., 1999), permuted MNIST – a version of MNIST that has the same fixed permutation applied to the pixels of all examples, and CIFAR-10 (Krizhevsky, 2009).

name.justification: The paper mentions meta-learning in the context of increasing data efficiency and identifying important training examples.
name.quote: It is a timely problem that has been the recent focus of few-shot learning approaches via meta-learning (Finn et al., 2017; Ravi & Larochelle, 2017).

name.justification: The paper explains that the CIFAR-10 experiments used a ResNet model, particularly for performance comparison.
name.quote: For CIFAR-10, we use a ResNet with cutout (De-Vries & Taylor, 2017) trained using SGD and momentum with a particular learning rate schedule.

is_contributed.justification: ResNet is a well-known existing neural network architecture widely used for image classification tasks and was used in this paper for conducting experiments.

is_compared.justification: The experiments are explicitly used to compare forgetting dynamics using ResNet and assessing generalization performance after removing certain training examples.
is_compared.quote: In Fig. 5 (Left), we show the evolution of the generalization performance in CIFAR-10 when we artificially remove examples from the training dataset.
